whyDutchCompanies.heading: Why Dutch companies choose us
whyDutchCompanies.para1: Most staffing options built for the Dutch market fall into one of two camps. Offshore agencies place talent in India, Malaysia, the Philippines, or Colombia — cheap, but you're managing time zone gaps and a candidate who doesn't know Dutch employment norms. Or you get compliance advisors built to help foreign companies set up payroll when entering the Netherlands — useful if you're a US company opening a Dutch office, useless if you're a Dutch company trying to hire.
whyDutchCompanies.para2: We're neither. We're built for Dutch companies, hiring Dutch and EU-based talent, in your time zone, under Dutch labor law, with both employment models — Payrolling and RPO — under one roof.

faqs.q: Is this legal under Dutch labor law?
faqs.a: Yes. With Payrolling, we're the legal employer of record — contracts, tax withholding, and statutory obligations are ours to handle, not yours. With RPO, the candidate is hired directly by you, under your own employment terms, so standard Dutch employment law applies as it would for any hire you make.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the role and the model. Payrolling pricing is based on the employee's gross salary plus a service fee; RPO pricing is typically a placement fee based on the role's salary band. We'll give you an exact number on a call once we know the role — we don't publish a flat rate because a Virtual Assistant and an AI Engineer aren't priced the same way.

hero.h1: Hire IT & development staff in the Netherlands
hero.subhead: Front-end to AI engineering — recruit developers directly, or lease payrolled IT staff. Ten roles, one point of contact.

sections.coverageBody:
Companies come to us for IT roles for three different reasons, and they're not interchangeable. Some are building a product and need developers who'll own a codebase long-term. Some have a working dev team with one gap — a QA specialist, a data engineer — that's slowing everything else down. Others need coverage: IT support, testing, maintenance work that has to happen but doesn't need a full-time hire on their own payroll.

IT & Development covers all three: front-end, back-end and full-stack development, mobile app development, data and AI/ML engineering, QA testing, IT support, and electrical engineering roles that sit inside technical teams.

sections.modelTitle: Payrolling vs RPO for this category
sections.modelBody: There's a real split here, but it runs by role type, not by the category as a whole. Core development roles — full-stack, back-end, mobile — tend to go through RPO: companies want that person as a permanent, direct hire, since they'll own product code long-term and institutional knowledge matters. Coverage and support roles — QA testing, IT support — more often go through Payrolling or Staff Outsourcing, since the need is real but doesn't always justify a permanent headcount addition. If you're not sure which side of that line your role falls on, that's exactly what the call is for.
sections.howItWorksBody: Same process as the rest of the site: you tell us the role, we shortlist candidates, you interview, you pick the model.

faqs.q: Do you vet for a specific tech stack, or just general skill level?
faqs.a: Specific stack. If you need someone who's worked in React and Node, or has production experience with a particular data pipeline tool, tell us on the call — we screen against that, not a generic "developer" profile.

faqs.q: We don't have a technical person in-house to assess candidates — how does vetting work then?
faqs.a: We handle the technical screening before anyone reaches your shortlist. You still run the interviews that matter to you — culture, communication, how they think through a problem — but you're not starting from zero on technical fit.

faqs.a: Depends on the niche — tell us what you need and we'll be straight with you about whether it's a fast search or a longer one.

faqs.q: Do you place both contract/temporary and permanent IT staff?
faqs.a: Yes — that's the Payrolling vs RPO split above. Same talent pool, different employment structure depending on what you need.

sections.coverageBody:
"Marketing" gets used as one word for jobs that don't actually overlap much. Someone has to run the channels day to day. Someone has to make what goes on them. Someone has to decide where the budget goes. And someone has to tell you, afterward, whether any of it worked. Those are four different skill sets, not one generalist role.

Marketing & Analytics covers execution (social, content), strategy (online marketing), and measurement (analytics, BI, data) — so you can hire for the specific gap you actually have, not a catch-all "marketing person."

sections.modelBody: There's a lean here, though it's worth confirming against real placements before we call it settled. Always-on execution roles — Social Media Manager, Content Creator — tend to work better as RPO hires, since someone running your channels day to day benefits from being an actual team member, not a rotating resource. Analytics and reporting roles — Google Analytics Specialist, Power BI Specialist, Data Analyst — more often suit Payrolling or Staff Outsourcing, since the need can be tied to a specific reporting cadence or project rather than a permanent seat. Online Marketer sits in between and depends on whether you're hiring for one campaign or an ongoing strategy role — worth flagging on the call.

hero.title: Recruitment Outsourcing for Dutch Companies

sections.conceptBody1: We search, screen, and shortlist candidates against the role you need filled. You interview whoever makes the shortlist. If someone's a fit, you extend the offer and they become your employee—not ours, not a leased worker, yours from day one.
sections.conceptBody2: This is different from Payrolling, where we stay the legal employer and the person works for you under our umbrella. Recruitment outsourcing (or recruitment/placement) is a one-time transaction: we do the sourcing work, you do the hiring.
sections.conceptBody3: It suits companies who know exactly what role they're filling and want full control over that person going forward—performance reviews, career development, how they fit the team long-term.

hero.title: Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) for Dutch Companies
hero.subtitle: If you're filling one role, you don't need RPO—you need Recruitment/Placement. RPO is for when hiring itself has become a problem: you're opening multiple roles at once, your internal team can't keep up with the pipeline, or you're scaling fast enough that ad-hoc hiring isn't cutting it anymore.

sections.conceptBody1: Recruitment process outsourcing means we don't just find you one person—we run the hiring process for you, on an ongoing basis, for as long as you need it.
sections.conceptBody2: Think of it less as "fill this vacancy" and more as "handle this part of our operation." We plug into how you hire—sourcing, screening, interview coordination, sometimes offer management—and run it at whatever volume you need.
sections.conceptBody3: With a single placement, you tell us what you need once, we deliver a shortlist, the engagement ends. RPO doesn't work that way. It's a standing arrangement: we act as an extension of your hiring function, working from your requirements on a continuous basis as new roles open up.
sections.noteBody: That might mean five hires this quarter and two next quarter. It might mean staffing an entire new department. Either way, you're not restarting the conversation every time—we already know your hiring bar, your process, and what "a good fit" looks like for your company.

sections.laborFooter: RPO takes more of the process off your plate than a single placement does—that's the point of it. But the actual employment relationship still sits with you, same as Recruitment/Placement. RPO isn't Payrolling; we're not the employer here either way.
sections.comparisonTitle: RPO vs. Recruitment/Placement: Which Fits You
sections.comparisonSubtitle: If you're filling one seat, RPO is overkill—you'd be paying for infrastructure built around volume you don't have.
sections.rpoDesc: RPO earns its cost when hiring becomes a repeated, sustained need—several roles at once, a new team getting built out, or hiring pace that's outstripping what your internal team can manage alone. The honest way to decide: if you can picture needing this again in three months for a different role, RPO probably fits.
sections.payrollDesc: Placement handles a single hire cleanly, without setting up an ongoing process for something that isn't recurring. If this is a one-off gap to fill, go with Recruitment/Placement instead and revisit RPO if hiring volume picks up.

hero.title: Temporary Staffing Services for Dutch Companies
hero.subtitle: Sometimes you don't need a permanent hire. You need someone for three months, or through a busy season, or to cover a role while you figure out if it needs to be permanent at all. That's what temporary staffing is for—extra hands, without the long-term commitment of a full hire.

sections.conceptBody1: We source, screen, and place someone with your team—but unlike Recruitment/Placement, they stay on our payroll, not yours. You get their day-to-day work; we handle the employment side: contracts, payroll, the administrative parts of having staff.
sections.conceptBody2: This matters most when your need has a shape to it—a defined project, a seasonal spike, covering parental leave, testing whether a role is even needed long-term before you commit to hiring for it.
sections.conceptBody3: If you already know this is a permanent role you want filled once and kept, this isn't the right page—go with Recruitment/Placement instead. Temporary staffing is built for flexibility, not for someone you're planning to keep for years.
sections.noteBody: We employ the person. You direct their work. When the project ends or your need shifts, the arrangement ends without you managing a termination process because you were never their employer to begin with.

hero.title: Payrolling for Dutch Companies
hero.subtitle: You've found someone you want working for your company—maybe through your own search, maybe through us—but you don't want to become their legal employer. Payrolling solves that: we hire the person on paper, you manage them day to day, and all the employer obligations sit with us instead of you.

sections.conceptBody1: We become the legal employer of record. Contract, payroll, tax withholding, statutory leave, pension contributions where applicable—all of it runs through us. You get full operational control: this person works on your team, follows your direction, does the job you need done.
sections.conceptBody2: What you don't take on is the administrative and legal weight of Dutch employment law. This is different from Recruitment/Placement, where the person becomes your direct employee outright.
sections.conceptBody3: Companies use this for a few different reasons: not having Dutch payroll infrastructure set up yet, wanting flexibility to scale headcount without the complexity of hiring and terminating directly, or simply preferring not to carry employer liability.
sections.noteBody: It's not temp work in the sense of "short-term cover." Payrolling can run indefinitely—someone can work with your team for years under this arrangement if that's what suits you. The difference from a direct hire isn't duration; it's who's legally responsible.

steps.desc: No fixed end date required. Scale down, extend, or convert to direct employment later if that becomes the right move.

ourApproach.heroSubtitle: A lot of staffing firms have a model they push because it's the one they're built around. We run two — recruitment/placement and payrolling — and the first real part of our job is figuring out which one actually solves your problem, not which one we'd rather sell you.
ourApproach.thinkingTitle: The model comes second. The problem comes first.

thinking.item1Desc: Before we talk roles, we ask what kind of gap you're actually filling. A permanent seat on your team needs a different approach than three months of coverage during a busy stretch.
thinking.item2Title: We'll tell you when we're not the right fit
thinking.item2Desc: If you need offshore staffing for cost reasons, or compliance advisory for setting up a Dutch entity, we're not that. We'd rather say so on the first call than take the work and underdeliver.
thinking.item3Desc: We place across six domains, not one. That's deliberate. Most companies don't have a single hiring need at a single point in time. The upside is that you don't need five vendors for five different roles.

ourApproach.workTitle: What this actually looks like day to day
ourApproach.workSubtitle: Our approach isn't just something we say. It shapes how we work with you from the first conversation onward.

work.item1Title: We vet before we shortlist, not after.
work.item1Desc: We focus on understanding whether a candidate actually fits the role before putting them in front of you.
